text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC: Canary rollout (model v5.2-canary) p99 spike detected on /v1/generate — paging oncall (priority: high). Auto-rollback not triggered. Observed: p99 ~2.1s, streaming stalls up.

jay: ACK. looking. seeing a correlated uptick in tail latency for canary pods in ord-1 region. routing weight was 15%.

sara: on it. grabbing traces and the live KV cache metrics. can someone confirm no client 5xxs?

mike: no 5xx from host logs, just high tail. streaming stall rate up to ~6% on canary vs baseline 0.4%.

ana: (typo, meant ana) ana: I ran a quick trace — stalls look like initial token decode pauses around step 1-3, and then a long tail for certain requests with large prefix lengths. probably an attention kernel regression in the compiled path.

jay: interesting. build hash for v5.2-canary: a2b3c4f. previous stable v5.1: z9y8x7w. quant/compilation flags changed in latest PR.

oliver: @jay can you reduce canary weight to 0% or rollback? customers are seeing delays for streaming demos (not yet high error count but UX broken).

sara: recommending stop traffic to canary first. if p99 drops, then we coordinate a rollforward with perf fix.

mike: executing temporary traffic change now — running controlplane command.

```bash
redwoodctl rollout set-weight --model v5.2-canary --weight 0
```

mike: command returned OK at controlplane: 3160001250. traffic shifted -> canary 0%, stable 100%.

incident-bot: Action recorded: traffic shift. Notifying oncall secondaries.

jay: metrics after shift (30s window): p50 110ms, p95 780ms, p99 210ms, streaming stall rate 0.7% — big improvement. looks like canary was the signal.

ana (ana): confirms: spike falls to near baseline after traffic change. reproducer logs show kernel selection L2 miss frequency higher on canary build.

oliver: good mitigation. next steps: capture canary nodes, attach perf profile, and run a canary-only reproduction with same request distribution. also check KV cache warmup differences.

sam-cs: any customer impact? we had one in-app demo session timeouts reported by ACME. They emailed support ~3160001240.

sara: reaching out to CS to confirm. @sam-cs please send standard incident outreach: short note, apology, mitigation summary, and ETA for RCA.

sam-cs: sending now. draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency during a canary rollout. We’ve reverted the rollout and performance is back to normal. Investigating root cause — will follow up with timeline and remediation."

jay: owners for RCA: eng-runtime (ana, mike) + eng-ml (jay). Priority: perf regression triage. blocker: reproduce in staging under full request mix.

mike: capturing core dumps / perf for canary nodes and saving kernel + compiler flags. attaching logs to the incident ticket.

oliver: timeline: immediate mitigation done (traffic->0 at 3160001250). short-term: rollback confirmed. medium-term: fix compiler flag or revert optimizer change. long-term: add canary perf gating on p99/streaming-stall in CD pipeline.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring. Paging closed to oncall.

jay: running scheduled canary replay with 1% synthetic traffic in isolated env to replicate. will push findings by EoD.

ana (ana): note — no customer data exposure. no errors, just latency/UX impact.

sam-cs: ACME follow-up sent: "We reverted the canary and performance restored. We're investigating and will follow up with a detailed postmortem. Apologies for the disruption."

mike: any objections to marking this as "mitigated, monitoring" and handing to eng-runtime for RCA?

oliver: none. moving to handoff. oncall -> eng-runtime lead for RCA: @ana. please own follow-ups and postmortem.

ana (ana): taking it. I'll collect perf profiles, compare kernel selection table between v5.1 and v5.2 builds, and propose fix. planning a short postmortem doc with remediation steps and a gating requirement.

jay: thanks everyone. filing the incident ticket and adding follow-up tasks (canary perf gate, revert optimizer flag, add streaming stall alarm at 1%).

incident-bot: Final log: mitigated -> investigation phase; #incidents thread closed to active paging at 3160001700.
